AI Overview

Marie Curie was a pioneering physicist and chemist who conducted groundbreaking research on radioactivity. She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize and the only woman to win Nobel Prizes in two scientific fields.

Curie discovered two new elements, polonium and radium, in 1898. During World War I, she developed mobile radiography units known as petroleuses to provide X-ray services to field hospitals.

Marie Curie Biography & Discoveries - Britannica

Marie Curie, Polish-born French physicist, famous for her work on radioactivity and twice a winner of the Nobel Prize.
